subject: SLO qualification: streaming latency & autoscale confirmation
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@fastpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-28T17:15:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: latency targets and burst behavior (post-demo)

Hi Vivek / Grace,

Thanks for the demo earlier — helpful walkthrough. A few clarifying items from our side so we can finish internal SRE scoping:

- Target SLOs: FastPay wants streaming p95 end-to-end latency <= 200ms for authorization flows (short prompts, ~20 tokens). We expect p50 ~40ms. Can Redwood validate these with our load profile?
- Baseline throughput: steady-state 600 concurrent streams (each stream is a live user flow). Peak bursts up to ~3,000 concurrent streams during promos.
- Scale-up: we need to understand typical scale-up times from idle -> handling +90% of burst. Target <45s for initial burst ramp if possible.
- Warm pools: what's the recommended prewarmed size (GPUs / instances) to achieve the target? Also behavior if warm pool exhausted (queueing/backpressure vs immediate fallback).
- Queueing: acceptable maximum queue wait for FastPay is 6s for auth calls; beyond that we prefer graceful degradation to a smaller fallback model.
- Measurement: can you provide the exact metrics you would use (p50/p95/p99 token latency, stream handshake, token generation rate) and a suggested test plan?

I've attached a brief internal traffic snapshot and our initial SLO matrix. Appreciate a short post-call recap and proposed next steps / M.A.P. (mutual action plan).

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
samir.rao@fastpay.com

Attachments: fastpay-traffic-snapshot.csv (attached), initial-slo-matrix.xlsx (attached)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@fastpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-29T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency targets and burst behavior (post-demo)

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Recap from our side and a proposed mutual action plan:

Recap (what we heard)
- Streaming p95 target <=200ms for ~20-token auth flows; p50 target ~40ms
- Steady 600 concurrent streams; bursts to ~3k concurrent streams
- Desired scale-up observable <45s and max queue wait <=6s with graceful fallback to smaller model if needed

What Redwood will validate / propose (deliverables)
1) Measurement plan & metrics (attached: slo-matrix-fastpay.xlsx) — we will measure: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, token-emit latency, stream handshake time, request->first-token, and queue wait time.
2) Burst test plan (attached: redwood-burst-testplan-v2.pdf) — synthetic ramp profiles to simulate promotions (ramp to peak in 60s, hold 90s, then decay).
3) Warm-pool sizing recommendation — initial recommendation: 18 prewarmed streams (GPU-backed) per 1,000 expected peak concurrent streams for the model family you tried. For your 3k peak that implies ~54 prewarmed streams as a starting point; we'll work with actual observed priming time during tests and adjust.
4) Fallback policy — queue with bounded wait (6s) + auto-fallback to a smaller quantized model if wait >6s or if we detect degraded tail.
5) Runbook for scale-up: target 30–45s to reach ~80–90% capacity when warm-pool seeding is used. If warm pool is empty, cold-starts can be 60–120s depending on model and hardware.

Proposed next steps / timeline
- Week 1 (May 6–10): sync on exact model variant and traffic mix; finalize test harness.
- Week 2 (May 13–17): capacity and burst tests in a controlled environment (we provide the script and collect observability).
- Week 3 (May 20–24): analyze results, adjust warm-pool sizing, and finalize SLO language for contract.

Notes on tradeoffs
- Prewarmed capacity reduces scale-up time significantly but has steady cost; we will include cost estimates in the test report.
- A smaller fallback model reduces user-perceived quality for some flows — we recommend reserving fallback for non-critical paths where acceptable.

Please confirm the proposed windows and whether FastPay wants Redwood to run tests in your private VPC (we can coordinate creds) or in a Redwood dedicated test project. Once you confirm, we'll lock dates.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-burst-testplan-v2.pdf, slo-matrix-fastpay.xlsx
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@fastpay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-29T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency targets and burst behavior (post-demo)

Adding a few technical specifics to help your SREs plan tests:

- Definitions: we treat a "concurrent stream" as an open streaming session (handshake + ongoing token emission). Concurrency measurements will be reported as live streams/sec and as concurrent connections.
- Warm pool behavior: prewarmed instances allocate model memory + run minimal priming tokens to populate KV cache. Typical priming latency observed: 12–18s on our 80GB A100 equivalents; full readiness (network libs, JIT) ~25–40s. That means a modest warm pool can reduce cold-start outliers to within your 45s requirement.
- Cold starts: if no warm pool, cold start to first-token ranges 60–120s depending on quantization and sequence length.
- Scale-up mechanics: with autoscaler + warm pool we target 30–45s to handle an abrupt 5x traffic spike for model variants we tested. For your burst profile (5x from 600 to 3k) we'll simulate two ramp profiles: aggressive (peak in 30s) and moderate (peak in 60s).
- Queueing policy: propose a hard cap on queue wait of 6s with token-level backpressure. If wait exceeds 6s, the request returns a structured fallback JSON indicating fallback_model=true and an abbreviated response.
- Observability: we will emit metrics with these keys: redwood.stream.p50_ms, redwood.stream.p95_ms, redwood.stream.p99_ms, redwood.stream.queue_wait_ms, redwood.stream.first_token_ms, redwood.stream.tokens_per_sec, and trace IDs for sampling. We'll share a Grafana dashboard and a short Prometheus scrape config.

I attached a sample warm-pool metrics CSV from a prior test for reference (warm-pool-metrics-sample.csv).

If this looks good we can have Marissa schedule the test windows and we'll provide the load generator config (locust + internal harness) and a simple contract SLO draft for legal to review.

- Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: warm-pool-metrics-sample.csv

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick confirmation and asks before we lock dates:

- FastPay confirms the windows (Week 2 May 13–17 for controlled burst tests). Please run both aggressive (30s ramp) and moderate (60s ramp) profiles.
- We prefer Redwood to run tests in our VPC (private) — please send the secure credential steps and any IP allowlist requirements.
- Legal: please include an SLO measurement clause for the contract draft: "p95 streaming latency measured across a rolling 30-day window; if p95 breaches the agreed target >2% of measurement buckets in the rolling window, FastPay is eligible for service credit per the contract." We will share FastPay legal contacts separately.
- Can you include a short sample Grafana output (png) and the raw csv of the test results in the post-test packet?

If you can attach the final test script and the DocuSign link for the test authorization, Marissa and I will confirm.

Thanks,
Samir
